questions.prompt: Why should you avoid KEYS on a large production database?

options.text: It is O(N) over the whole keyspace and can block the server for everyone
It only works on string values
It requires authentication that SCAN does not

questions.explanation: KEYS scans every key in one command, and since commands run in a single thread, that can block all other clients on a big keyspace. Use SCAN instead.

questions.prompt: How do you know a SCAN iteration is complete?

options.text: When it returns an empty array of keys
When it returns the same keys twice
SCAN always finishes in a single call

questions.explanation: SCAN is cursor-based: you pass the returned cursor back on each call, and iteration is finished when the cursor comes back as 0 (an individual call may return zero keys but a non-zero cursor).

questions.prompt: Which statements about Redis Strings are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: They are binary-safe and can hold up to 512 MB
INCR works only if the current value parses as an integer
A plain SET keeps any existing TTL by default
MSET and MGET operate on several keys in one command

questions.explanation: Strings are binary-safe up to 512 MB; INCR errors on non-integers; MSET/MGET are multi-key. A plain SET CLEARS the TTL unless you pass KEEPTTL.

questions.prompt: What does `SET lock:job1 "owner" NX` return if lock:job1 already exists?

options.text: (nil) — NX refuses to set because the key exists
(error) — NX is not a valid option

questions.explanation: NX means 'only set if the key does not exist.' When the key already exists, SET does nothing and returns (nil).

questions.prompt: The command that atomically increases the integer stored at a key by 1 is ______. (one word)
questions.explanation: INCR adds 1 atomically (creating the key as 0 first if needed). Because it's a single command, concurrent increments never lose counts.

questions.prompt: Match each command to what it does.

pairs.right: Reports whether a key is present
Adds to a string and returns the new length
Adds a floating-point amount to a number

questions.explanation: EXISTS checks presence, TYPE reports the type, APPEND extends a string (returning its new length), and INCRBYFLOAT does floating-point addition.
